prompt:
Gentle storybook painterly illustration, realism about 3.5/5, soft gouache-and-oil brushwork, warm-hearted and calm, natural NEUTRAL daylight with true colours, off-white whites, no orange, sepia, amber or golden cast, no pink or blue tint, clear readable figures with contact shadows on the floor, consistent eye-level perspective, 16:9 wide composition.
Scene: Cabinet médical in the B17_cabinet building, outdoors. Camera: on the square's cobbles in front of the townhouse, facing west.
Setting: tall three-storey cream stone townhouse, sage-green shutters, a wrought-iron first-floor balcony curled like a giant stethoscope, a chimney shaped like a big thermometer, an attic dormer, a brass bell-pull at the green front door; floor: pale grey cobbles of the square, herb pots on the steps. Landmark: the stethoscope-shaped balcony railing and thermometer chimney. Light: same spring late-morning daylight as the square. The room feels lived-in and real, with depth (never an empty white backdrop).
Paint these exits clearly as walkable openings: the green front door up three steps, CENTRE (way to La salle d'attente); the cobbled foreground at the bottom left (the way back out).
Also paint a narrow lane on the RIGHT with a small side door (a street mouth).
Leave a blank light board for the room sign high on the back wall. No written words, letters, numbers or logos anywhere (signs and plaques are blank boards). No blood, no wounds, no needles in skin (syringes only as capped harmless props), no alcohol, no smoking, no religious symbols, no red-cross emblem. Nobody cropped by the image edge; keep every figure well inside the frame with a clear gap between figures. Figures stand on the floor or sit on real furniture, never floating or in rows behind a counter.
